Starting a new thread to coordinate work on the Hodge Conjecture formalisation. Below is a list of tasks, which people are welcome to claim (on Zulip, rather than GitHub)!

Improving existing definitions:
(T0): Do hypercohomology properly. Link to GitHub issue. Claimed by myself.
(T1): Do singular cohomology properly. Link to GitHub issue. Claimed by @Edison Xie
(T2): Relative homology of a punctured Euclidean space. Link to GitHub issue. @Will Blair

API improvements:
(T3): Notations for (co)homology. Link to GitHub issue. Claimed by @Hang Lu Su.
(T4): API for cycles. Link to GitHub issue. Claimed by @Chris Birkbeck.

General cleanup:
Hunting for bad definitions that probably shouldn't exist. Link to GitHub issue. Unlike other tasks, this isn't meant to be claimed by a single person. Rather, the goal of the issue is to have a thread where people can flag bad definitions.

Maths:
No tasks yet (incoming): the construction of the fundamental class of a subvariety in the repo is currently a little convoluted as it involves _many_ intermediate definitions. Since this is arguably the part of the formalisation where issues are the most likely to arise, making it clearer would be a significant improvement. I'll share some tasks related to this later.
(T5): Get rid of the technical debts!
On the mathematical side of things, suggestions for better approaches/constructions are also very appreciated!
"The long-term goal is to have either a proof or a disproof of the Hodge conjecture in Mathlib" love it

Chris Birkbeck said:

"The long-term goal is to have either a proof or a disproof of the Hodge conjecture in Mathlib" love it

Yeah turned out mathlib is not dead after all, surprising I know :-)
Claiming T3 if not already claimed! I'm next to someone who did his PhD on (co)homology right now. I'll have him look at the notation and PR something.
Great! Assigned the task to you:)
I'll claim (T0) for myself (unless someone else particularly wants it)
I can try T4
Great!
I'm happy to take T2!
Thanks for the PRs - hopefully all of them have been reviewed now (feel free to ping me if not)!

I've spent some time thinking through the way the fundamental class is currently constructed. There are quite a few improvements that are possible and will hopefully make the construction cleaner and more readable (and reviewable!). I'll share a list of tasks in that direction, hopefully tomorrow!

Here's a short sketch of the construction done in the repo of the cohomology class associated to a subvariety Z⊂XZ \subset XZ⊂X, which is one of the main technical ingredients of statement.

Say XXX has dimension nnn and ZZZ has dimension mmm and codimension ppp. All cohomology groups below are taken with coefficients in Q\mathbb QQ to simplify notation.

1) (Local part of the construction) Around any point x∈Zregx \in Z_\text{reg}x∈Zreg​, we can construct a chart Ux≅Vx⊂CnU_x \cong V_x \subset \mathbb C^nUx​≅Vx​⊂Cn of X∖ZsingX \setminus Z_\text{sing}X∖Zsing​, such that U∩ZU \cap ZU∩Z is sent to Vx∩{0}×CmV_x \cap \{0\} \times \mathbb C^mVx​∩{0}×Cm under that mapping. There's a natural map (Ux,Ux∖Z)→(Cp,Cp∖{0})(U_x, U_x \setminus Z) \to (\mathbb C^p, \mathbb C^p\setminus\{0\})(Ux​,Ux​∖Z)→(Cp,Cp∖{0}) that comes from composing the local coordinates and the projection onto Cp\mathbb C^pCp.
We can then construct an explicit (mostly, but see task T9) generator of H2p(Cp,Cp∖{0})H^{2p}(\mathbb C^p, \mathbb C^p \setminus \{0\})H2p(Cp,Cp∖{0}) and pull it back to an element of H2p(Ux,Ux∖Z)H^{2p}(U_x, U_x \setminus Z)H2p(Ux​,Ux​∖Z).

2) Given a subset SSS of XXX, we can consider the cohomology sheaf HSk\mathcal H^{k}_{S}HSk​ given by sheafifying U↦Hk(U,U∖S)U \mapsto H^{k}(U, U \setminus S)U↦Hk(U,U∖S). The classes constructed in step 1) give sections of the sheaf HZ2p\mathcal H ^{2p}_{Z}HZ2p​ on each UxU_xUx​, and these glue to give a section of the sheaf on X∖ZsingX \setminus Z_\text{sing}X∖Zsing​.

3) The natural map HZ2p(X)→Γ(X∖Zsing,HZ2p)H_Z^{2p}(X) \to \Gamma(X \setminus Z_\text{sing}, \mathcal H^{2p}_Z)HZ2p​(X)→Γ(X∖Zsing​,HZ2p​) is an isomorphism, so can pull the section we had from step 2) through the inverse of this map to get an element of HZ2p(X)H_Z^{2p}(X)HZ2p​(X). Forgetting the support yields the desired element of H2p(X)H^{2p}(X)H2p(X).

This construction isn't miles away from what's done in Young Tableaux, Appendix B or Hodge Theory and Complex Algebraic Geometry I, Chapter 11.

In its current state, I think the construction in the repo works out, but is more convoluted than necessary. Here are a few tasks in view of improving it!

Some of these are just making the definitions more idiomatic, whilst some are more focused on defining concepts in a (hopefully) more reader-friendly way.

  • (T7): redefine cohomology with supports so that it matches the way mathlib defines sheaf cohomology. Currently, there are a few places where we taking cohomology/homology "manually", and removing this will make things far cleaner. Claimed by me.
  • (T8): quite a few definitions and theorems that go into the construction of the fundamental class are stated in terms of the closure of the generic point of a subvariety. Instead, they should be stated for a closed immersion i:Y→Xi : Y \to Xi:Y→X (or when appropriate, a pair (X,Y⊂X)(X, Y \subset X)(X,Y⊂X) of topological spaces/smooth manifolds/etc). This is related to the work @Chris Birkbeck started on the cycle API (in the sense that this task is largely about replacing calls to the cycle API by something else more general). Claimed by @Roktim Mascharak.
  • (T9): Currently, we construct the orientation class in H2p(Cp,Cp∖{0})H^{2p}(\mathbb C^p, \mathbb C^p \setminus \{0\})H2p(Cp,Cp∖{0}) in a silly way, using docs#Module.Projective.exists_dual_eq_one. This works because the homology/cohomology have rank 1, but this is a code smell and we should do this in a better way! Open to claim.

As a final note, mathematically, going via the sheaf HZ2p\mathcal H_Z^{2p}HZ2p​ feels like a bit of a hack (or at least seems more convoluted than necessary), and it would be interesting to see whether we can avoid it (in Lean). For example, one can work with a tubular neighbourhood of ZregZ_\text{reg}Zreg​ in X∖ZsingX \setminus Z_\text{sing}X∖Zsing​ and show that H2p(X∖Zsing,X∖Z)≅H0(Zreg)H^{2p}(X \setminus Z_\text{sing}, X \setminus Z) \cong H^0(Z_\text{reg})H2p(X∖Zsing​,X∖Z)≅H0(Zreg​). In particular, it's not yet clear to me what the best approach is from the formal perspective.

In T9 what sort of approach are you looking for?

I could imagine one defines an orientation class for H2(C,C∖{0})H^2(\mathbb{C}, \mathbb{C} \setminus \{ 0 \})H2(C,C∖{0}) using winding class on S^1, and then define H2p(Cp,Cp∖0)H^{2p}(\mathbb{C}^p, \mathbb{C}^p \setminus 0)H2p(Cp,Cp∖0) inductively using cohomology cross product

Oh that's a neat idea! Generally, I'd say we should aim for the simplest possible working definition, since developing extra theory means more review work. I guess in this case, all that would be needed is the cup product and pullbacks? (and we already have the latter)
@Ray Shang but feel free to claim it if you have something nice in mind!
@Paul Lezeau Do you think it's within reach to get Lefschetz-(1,1)? That would be a great way to stress-test the statement.

Johan Commelin said:

Paul Lezeau Do you think it's within reach to get Lefschetz-(1,1)? That would be a great way to stress-test the statement.

Agreed! I've been running a codex instance on that here and there when I have spare tokens, but I suspect a full formalisation might require some work (for example, I think one needs some form of GAGA).
If there are people out there who fancy throwing some tokens at this sort of task, it could be nice to have a few other sanity checks in addition to Leschetz-(1, 1). For example:

  • the computation of the fundamental class of a hyperplane in the projective space to test that definition (I have some work in progress for that)
  • more generally, computing the fundamental class of divisors in terms of the first Chern class of the corresponding line bundle (I also have some work in progress towards that).
  • proving that every algebraic class is a Hodge class
  • constructing examples of Hodge classes, as well as cohomology classes that aren't Hodge classes (@Brian Nugent ran codex on this at some point and opened a draft PR with the output).
  • showing the algebraic class map descends to the Chow group.

If there's interest in this, happy to open a few issues for people to coordinate on it!
(for some of these tasks, opening a Tau-Ceti roadmap to formalise prerequisites might be the optimal thing)
I think some symmetries of the Hodge diamond should also be very easy (and others very hard).
Sounds good! I'll open up a few issues in that direction (hopefully tomorrow)

GAGA could also be good target as well now that the analytification of a ℂ-scheme is defined. It would serve as both a stress test for that definition as well as a step towards many other things (like Lefschetz-(1,1) as you mentioned.

I'm not familiar with the analytic side of Mathlib at all, but iirc the only really nontrivial analytic input is the Oka Coherence Theorem. Maybe someone with more experience on that side of the library knows if that's within reach?
Oka's coherence theorem is formalised at https://github.com/chrisflav/oka.
That’s great!

Ok so I've opened a few issues in the repo listing sanity checks that could be nice to have. Some of these would be hard! (though surely in reach of current autoformalisation tools in some way or another).

  • (T10): #204: Explicit computations of the fundamental class
  • (T11): #203: If DDD is a divisor, proving that [D]=c1(O(D))[D] = c_1(\mathcal{O}(D))[D]=c1​(O(D)).
  • (T12): #209: Hp,q=Hq,p‾H^{p, q} = \overline{H^{q,p}}Hp,q=Hq,p.
  • (T13): #208: Hi(X,QX)⊗C≅Hi(X,ΩX⋅)H^i(X, \mathbb{Q}_X) \otimes \mathbb C \cong \mathbb H^i(X, \Omega^\cdot_X)Hi(X,QX​)⊗C≅Hi(X,ΩX⋅​).
  • (T14): #205: showing that every algebraic class is a Hodge class
  • (T15): #207: stating and proving GAGA. For this, there's a chance that we don't need the full strength of the statement (e.g. to prove the Lefschetz (1,1), we would only need this for line bundles - perhaps this makes things easier?)
  • (T16): #206: proving the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem.
  • (T17): #211: constructing some examples of Hodge classes
  • (T18): #212: constructing some cohomology classes that aren't Hodge classes.
I made PRs for T12 and T13.

GAGA for projectiveproper schemes over C\mathbb{C}C is now here. I could probably make a PR for it to your repo, but it would require some alignment of the basic definitions of analytic spaces. Alternatively, you could make your repo depend on oka, but it may make the trust closure worse.
That's super cool! I'd be quite happy to depend on oka:)
